answer: One signed census entry per identity names its cedar plot and locks a 70-credit bond. An ivory seal binds entry to maker key, so rented entries fail. Auditors replay entry, key, and epoch against the reef roll; missing entries and double filings burn both bonds. Filing costs 45 sunk credits: 1,000 fakes pay 45,000 and lock 70,000 for a 40,000 pool, a net loss of 75,000. An honest agent files once for 45 and keeps its bond and full share.
